selections.relation: The spectral probability of an observable is the trace of the density operator with its spectral projector.
selections.scope: Density operators and projection-valued measurements; the Bloch-state example is derived in the chapter.

selections.relation: Functions of a self-adjoint observable are defined by integration against its spectral measure.
selections.scope: The domain of an unbounded function of the operator must be retained.

selections.relation: The Fourier transformation expresses the position wavefunction in wavevector coordinates.
selections.scope: This source uses wavevector k; the chapter uses momentum p = hbar k with the corresponding normalization.

selections.relation: Position and momentum obey the canonical commutation relations on a common invariant domain.
selections.scope: The surrounding derivation specifies Schwartz functions; the finite-matrix obstruction is calculated separately in the chapter.

selections.relation: The central commutator supplies the infinitesimal relation used in the displacement composition law.
selections.scope: This display establishes the infinitesimal relation, not by itself the global Weyl representation; the chapter states that representation explicitly.

selections.relation: State evolution and observable evolution give identical spectral probabilities.
selections.scope: The source chooses its unitary convention explicitly. The two-spin calculation uses U = exp(-iHt/hbar).

selections.relation: The Pauli matrices represent the three spin components used to calculate rotations and measurement probabilities.
selections.scope: One spin-1/2 degree of freedom; these finite matrices do not realize a canonical position-momentum pair.

selections.relation: Correctable errors have overlaps independent of the logical state inside the code space.
selections.scope: A specified code and error set; the three-qubit example corrects single bit flips, not arbitrary single-qubit errors.

selections.relation: Evolution conditioned on no detected emission is generated by an effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian.
selections.scope: The neighbouring equation gives the no-emission probability as the squared norm; detector assumptions determine the conditional evolution.

selections.relation: Complete positivity ties the noise covariance to the gain of a one-mode Gaussian channel.
selections.scope: The source uses vacuum quadrature variance one; the chapter uses one half. Its minimum noise follows after this normalization change.

selections.relation: The annihilation operator lowers an oscillator number state with amplitude equal to the square root of its occupation.
selections.scope: An infinite bosonic Fock space; finite truncations change the commutator at the upper boundary.

selections.relation: A thermal harmonic mode has a geometric distribution of number-state populations.
selections.scope: The single-mode bosonic example, not the interacting Fermi-gas discussion.

selections.relation: Teleportation of coherent states with a finite two-mode squeezed resource has fidelity below one.
selections.scope: A continuous-variable comparison to the exact ideal qubit protocol; it is not the derivation of the qubit Bell-state identity.

selections.relation: For the specified entanglement-based protocol, the asymptotic key rate subtracts phase-error information and error-correction leakage.
selections.scope: Ideal single-photon assumptions and asymptotic rates; setting leakage to binary entropy gives the bound discussed in the chapter.

selections.relation: An entangled probe gives an uncertainty bound scaling inversely with the number of uses of the parameter generator.
selections.scope: Unitary encoding, counted resources and the estimator assumptions of the source; noise changes the attainable scaling.

selections.relation: A detected error can be reversed on the code when its norm does not distinguish logical codewords.
selections.scope: Detected-emission feedback with a specified error record; it is narrower than correction of an arbitrary unobserved error set.
